findings.antecedent: Historic city (as a model)
findings.consequent: Sustains walkable, energy-efficient environments and resilient, mixed-use economies
findings.quote: For its advocates the historic city is a source of inspiration: a high-density model that sustains a walkable, energy efficient environ- ment and resilient, mixed-use economy.

findings.antecedent: Historic city image (as a vision for the future)
findings.consequent: Offers no vision of the future, stands contrary to actual history of many contemporary cities, affected by social/economic blight and physical deterioration, indicates irreversible decline
findings.quote: For the sceptics, such an image offers no vision of the future because it stands contrary to the actual history of many contemporary cities where old centres have been affected by social and eco- nomic blight usually accompanied by acute physical deterioration.

findings.antecedent: Need for understanding 21st-century urban requirements
findings.consequent: Requires radical thinking of conventional urban models
findings.quote: Instead, they propose, a radical thinking of conventional urban models is required to understand what will be needed in the twenty- first century.

findings.antecedent: Dense, information-rich settlements
findings.consequent: Humans would opt to live there
findings.quote: Edward Glaeser's argument that – all things being equal – humans would opt to live in dense, information-rich settlements, belongs (broadly speaking) in the Jane Jacobs tradition (Glaeser, 2001).

findings.antecedent: Dispersed agglomerations of built form and highly mobile populations in contemporary urban regions
findings.consequent: Necessitates new ways of conceiving 'the urban' for better understanding and design
findings.quote: However, other voices such as Thomas Sieverts assert that new ways of conceiving of 'the urban' are nece- ssary in order to fully understand and better design for the dispersed agglomerations of built form that are the characteristic milieu of highly mobile populations living in contemporary urban regions in the developed world (Sieverts, 2003).

findings.antecedent: Dense industrial city
findings.consequent: Considered a 'problem' requiring a 'solution' involving large open spaces within an extended urban fabric
findings.quote: With some license, we might put Sieverts in the tradition of Ebenezer Howard or Lewis Mumford for whom the dense industrial city was a 'problem' requiring a 'solution' in which the accommodation of large open spaces within an extended urban fabric would play an important part.

findings.antecedent: Internet and widespread availability of portable telecommunication devices
findings.consequent: Created a new 'digital layer' whose relationship with corporeal rhythms of urban space is unclear
findings.quote: The revolution in social and working practices associated with the internet and the widespread availability of portable telecommunication devices has created a new ‘digital layer'. The relationship of this aspatial (or 'transpatial') network with the corporeal rhythms of urban space is as yet far from clear.

findings.antecedent: Global trends
findings.consequent: Cities are more popular than ever before
findings.quote: The traditional urbanists undoubtedly have a point in claiming that globally speaking cities are more popular than ever before.

findings.consequent: World's urban population percentage expected to rise from 10% to 75%
findings.quote: In 1900, approximately 10 per cent of the world's popu- lation inhabited cities; by 2050 this number is expected to rise to 75 per cent (Burdett and Sudjic, 2007).

findings.antecedent: Time and different historical-geographical contexts
findings.consequent: City form and social life are fundamentally changed
findings.quote: However, this argument should not be taken to imply that the form and social life of the city are fundamentally unchanged over time and in different historical-geographical contexts.

findings.antecedent: Idealizing the historical city as a universally applicable model OR imposing inappropriate contemporary schemes onto complex urban tissues
findings.consequent: Stunts innovation OR creates danger to urban tissues
findings.quote: From a design perspective, there is as much danger in stunting innovation by idealizing the historical city as a universally applicable model as there is in imposing inappropriate contemporary schemes onto complex urban tissues that have evolved over many centuries.

findings.antecedent: Grand modernist narratives of architecture and urban design
findings.consequent: Associated with the destruction of highly valued historical urban forms, leading to suspicion in postmodern social theory
findings.quote: Part of the 'postmodern condition' in western social theory is manifested in a suspicion of the grand modernist narratives of architecture and urban design, which have become associated with the destruction of those historical urban forms that are (now) highly valued.

findings.antecedent: Planning for the future
findings.consequent: Requires a 'vision thing' as a necessary part of the design process
findings.quote: Nevertheless, in planning for the future, it is hard to do without the 'vision thing' entirely – as a necessary part of the design process.

findings.antecedent: Views of those who 'leave things alone' versus those who see opportunities from top-down interventions
findings.consequent: Often incommensurate, leading to conflict
findings.quote: It is probably inevitable therefore, that the views of those who would rather 'leave things alone' are often incommen- surate with those who see greater opportunities arising from top-down interventions.

findings.antecedent: Huge Olympic developments in East London
findings.consequent: Caused displacement or disadvantaging of many existing local amenities and small businesses
findings.quote: Much of the row over the huge Olympic developments in East London and their much-trumpeted 'legacy' for the local community has taken place on these terms – the cost being the displacement or disadvantaging of many existing local amenities and small businesses.

findings.antecedent: Historical areas
findings.consequent: Some are more privileged than others, not necessarily serving those most in need by local populations
findings.quote: Certainly, some historical areas seem to be more privileged than others and not necessarily the ones that matter most to the local populations who have the greatest need of them.

findings.antecedent: Highly mobile existence (especially if unable to easily separate from or maintain offline relationships via digital networks)
findings.consequent: Can be an alienating experience
findings.quote: Although a highly mobile existence can liberate individuals from the weight of history, it can also be an alienating experience – especially if you are whether the two can ever be easily separated (or indeed, whether they should be) as such networks are often used to maintain relationships made offline.

findings.antecedent: 'Edge city' developments
findings.consequent: Offer great economic opportunity but at potential cost to the sense of 'being at home'
findings.quote: 'Edge city' developments no doubt offer great economic opportunity, but at what potential cost to that sense of being 'at home'?

findings.antecedent: Historic city model
findings.consequent: Preference for it can be justified in highly pragmatic terms, not just nostalgia
findings.quote: All this may sound like so much advocacy of the historic city model, but the point is rather to highlight: first, that a preference for the milieu of the historic city does not have to be justified on grounds of chocolate-box nostalgia, indeed it can be expressed in highly pragmatic terms;

findings.antecedent: Complexity and formative role of the historic city in modern, mobile, and digitally networked lives
findings.consequent: Should not be casually reduced to a one-dimensional tourist destination
findings.quote: and second, to illustrate why the whole com- plexity of the historic city should not be casually reduced to that of a one-dimensional tourist destination when it is able to play such a for- mative role in 'modern lives' that are both highly mobile and digitally networked, as personally and professionally speaking is certainly the case with my hosts in Canterbury.

findings.antecedent: Still-functioning historic city
findings.consequent: Makes everyday living relatively light, freeing up time for other things
findings.quote: a still-functioning his- toric city makes relatively light the everyday work of living – such that one has simply more time for other things. Surely few qualities can be more important?

findings.antecedent: Indoor 'public' spaces of Mass Transit Railway Stations (Hong Kong)
findings.consequent: Comprise increasingly important aspects of life in large cities, raising questions about what constitutes 'public' space
findings.quote: On the basis of a number of case studies, Xue argues that such spaces comprise increasingly important aspects of life in large cities – though, as he acknowledges, this raises serious questions about what exactly is recog- nized as 'public' space.

findings.antecedent: Urban morphology and vernacular urban forms
findings.consequent: Can usefully inform urban design to better understand adaptation to local climatic conditions for energy efficiency
findings.quote: His short article suggests that urban design could be usefully informed by urban morphology in order to better understand how vernacular urban forms adapt to local climatic conditions, as large-scale archi- tectural projects have not traditionally prioritized such issues.

findings.antecedent: Increased neighbourhood density and pedestrian accessibility
findings.consequent: Tend to create economic value, supporting walkability from an economic standpoint
findings.quote: On the basis of research that includes a statistical analysis of property prices across a range of land uses, their study suggests that increased neighbourhood density and pedestrian accessibility tend to create economic value.

findings.antecedent: Multi-scale classification model (FUS-ion)
findings.consequent: Can help address design difficulties for creating 'liveable streets' on major intra-settlement routes
findings.quote: The authors draw on research from a case study of Perth, Australia, to test how their multi-scale classification model (FUS-ion) can help address this issue. Their work is a useful contribution to the growing literature concerned with how major network infrastructure can be made more effective for users across urban scales – and particularly at the human scale.

findings.antecedent: UK's new National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF 2012)
findings.consequent: Needs to function as successful urban design guidance while negotiating difficulties in creating a centralized regulatory regime for localized planning
findings.quote: Paterson's work draws on a wide range of academic, professional and community-based authorities to enquire into exactly what the new NPPF needs to do in order to function as successful urban design guidance, while at the same time negotiating the self-evident difficulties in creating a centralized regulatory regime for localized planning and design governance.

findings.antecedent: Simplified images of the urban past or visions of futurity that do not acknowledge historical dialogue between 'new' and 'old'
findings.consequent: Urban designers and societies cannot afford to be held hostage to them
findings.quote: urban designers (and urban societies) cannot afford to be hostage either to simplified images of the urban past or visions of futurity that do not acknowledge that in historical time the 'new' is always a dialogue with the 'old'.

findings.antecedent: The right to the social space of the city (when one needs recourse to it)
findings.consequent: Is still something to be valued, even in a world of global capital transfer, accelerated transit, and virtual spaces
findings.quote: the right to the social space of the city – that is, when one needs recourse to it is still something to be valued.

findings.antecedent: Virtual spaces and physical spaces
findings.consequent: Are not mutually exclusive, and the emergence of one does not have to imply the annihilation of the other
findings.quote: After all, none of these spaces is mutually exclusive and the emergence of one does not have to imply the annihilation of the other.
